operating_notes.text: Approved the price of Washed Coking Coal effective April 1, 2026 at ₹13,403/- per MT for Washed Prime Coking Coal and ₹10,937/- per MT for Washed Medium Coking Coal.
April 2026 raw coal production was 1.99 MT (opencast 1.92 MT, underground 0.07 MT) against 3.39 MT a year earlier.
April 2026 offtake of 2.26 MT exceeded production of 1.99 MT, indicating stock drawdown.
April 2026 overburden removal was 9.03 million CuM, down 51.7% from 18.71 million CuM a year earlier.
On May 02, 2026, four consumer-engaged workers died in a slurry slide at Heap No. C during slurry loading at Moonidih Washery, which is under renovation.
Commercial operations of the 2.0 MTPA Bhojudih Coal Washery commenced under the BOM model.
Operations at New Benedih Patch were stopped temporarily following a fatal accident caused by a haul road edge slide during heavy rainfall.
May 2026 raw coal production was 2.28 MT, down 25.5% YoY.
Approved interim diesel price variation for eligible Hiring of HEMM and Coal Transportation contracts.
Rationalised basic prices of certain grades of raw coking coal for the non-regulated sector with increases of approximately 0.1% to 14%.
Q2FY27 other income of ₹158.57 Cr was 85.4% of profit before tax of ₹185.78 Cr.
H1FY27 operating cash flow was ₹777.16 Cr, helped by ₹757.80 Cr released from trade receivables and ₹405.13 Cr from inventories.
Bhojudih washery (2.0 MTPA) started commercial operations on 26-05-2026.
Maheshpur RLS Project (5.0 MTPA) became operational on 20.09.2026.
H1FY27 sales realization hit an all-time high of ₹10,259.63 Cr.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹3,282.95 Cr, net profit ₹27.28 Cr.
Bharat Coking Coal received interim protection from the Revisional Authority against ₹17,344.46 Cr mining demand notices.
BCCL reported provisional April 2026 raw coal production of 1.99 MT; with offtake at 2.26 MT
Fatal accident at Moonidih Washery claimed four lives during slurry loading; no production impact expected as plant is under renovation.
Bharat Coking Coal withdrew its 2017 petition in the Jharkhand High Court regarding a 1998 industrial dispute order on May 7, 2026.
Bharat Coking Coal commenced commercial operations of its 2.0 MTPA Bhojudih Coal Washery under the BOM model.
Bharat Coking Coal reported a fatal accident at the New Benedih patch on May 29, 2026, resulting in temporary suspension of operations at the patch.

Bharat Coking Coal disclosed a ₹7,64,640 BSE fine (dated 27 May 2026) for board and committee composition breaches under SEBI LODR; its board on 30 May 2026 decided to seek a waiver and pursue independent director appointments with the Ministry of Coal.
Bharat Coking Coal approved interim measures for diesel price variation to mitigate financial stress in outsourced HEMM and coal transportation contracts.
Bharat Coking Coal approved the rationalisation of basic prices for certain non-regulated sector raw coking coal grades with increases up to 14%.
BCCL lost its Supreme Court appeal on October 8, 2026, and was ordered to pay ₹46.2 Cr in a contractual dispute.
On October 8, 2026, the National Green Tribunal disposed of an environmental application against BCCL, noting parallel proceedings in the Jharkhand High Court.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹4,412.58 Cr, net profit ₹123.74 Cr.
Bharat Coking Coal reported a Q2FY27 turnaround with PBT of ₹185.78 Cr and record H1 sales realizations of ₹10,260 Cr.
